docs.title: MASTER VIEW 2.0 — Design Doc
docs.status: DRAFT rev 4 — Rob reviewed the visual mockup ("not bad for a Master View") and his amendments are folded: always-full 3-phase layouts, phase lifecycle triggers, P4 inline-edit, Master-Admin edit-anything, owner-who-is-also-rep, kickoff steps replacing Met. OQ-1..5 resolved; awaiting final sign-off (Q39 gate)
docs.lead: each section leads with THE DECISION in one or two lines. Details, evidence, and quotes follow. Skim the bold lines and you have the whole design in two minutes.

sections.heading: Purpose statement — what the Master View is FOR
sections.decision: the Master View is Rob's operating picture, not a bigger rep screen. One glance answers four questions: (1) what phase is every customer in and what's lit, (2) who owes what / who's been invoiced and paid, (3) where the equity and spinoffs sit (owners-only), (4) what needs Rob's touch today. The rep view stays "only what closes deals." Anything that doesn't answer one of those four questions gets demoted or removed from the master surfaces.
points: There are THREE audiences, not two
Master View vs Rep View vs Customer portal, one table

sections.heading: Object taxonomy — Companies vs People
sections.decision: kill the interleaved "People ledger." Ship two list views — /companies and /people — each with columns tuned to its object. The network graph keeps mixed nodes (Rob explicitly likes that).
points: Name · Vertical · Status · Phase (P1 ●●○○) · Owed/Paid · Assigned rep · Last touch
Prospect · Client · Partner Org · Spinoff · Vertical Anchor · Dormant

sections.heading: Company record page spec
sections.decision: the company page is the delivery + money page. Order: header → Things to Address → Phase Blueprint tracker → People here → Deals (services / equity split) → Activity → Notes (human) → details grid → enrichment (collapsed, last). Rob: "You have the exact same page for the entity and the person when I click into them. That doesnt seem to make sense." Correct — today app/people/[id]/page.tsx renders the identical PersonEditor for both with only a "business" pill. That ends here.
points: All three phases ALWAYS render as FULL sections (Rob mockup amendment, 2026-07-22): even a not-started phase shows its complete fillable layout — component slots (unlit), money row placeholders (no agreement yet · not invoiced), the works — never a slim summary card
Per-phase section spec (master view — P2/P3 render this same full structure with empty slots)
Component lights; ALL lit = phase complete
Lights flip on a signal from partner tools (webhook), never hand-toggled once armed
Per-phase invoice/paid state, cross-checkable phase ↔ agreement ↔ invoice
One phase at a time is the norm
"Top Automations next" slot between P1 and P2

sections.heading: Person record page spec
sections.decision: the person page is relationship-forward — who they are, what they are to us, which company, who brought them, what they've opened — not a money/delivery page. Order: header (name · relationship label · role @ company link) → Things to Address → attribution lineage (full chain, §5) + doors opened → activity/notes → details grid → enrichment collapsed.

sections.heading: Attribution lineage component
sections.decision: every attribution line renders the full chain from ROB (origin) to the node, breadcrumb-style: ROB → Alex → Sarah → this company — compact, each hop clickable, computed by walking referredById to the root. BUILD-QUEUE Q39(e): "attribution lines must show the FULL referral chain back to ROB origin... never make Rob guess the origin node."
points: Computation (pure function, lib/lineage.ts, unit-tested per CR-3)

sections.heading: Phase-4 registry view (owners-only)
sections.decision: a dedicated /registry (owners-only) table — one row per spinoff/equity position — plus the owners-only equity section on each company page. Structured fields, never notes-crammed. Rob (7.22.26-2): "we will typically spin this up into a new entity and get an equity split. Calebs CRM is one example. Alex's HomeCloneVault is another... with Homevault, we have agreed to a 40/60 Split... we have not signed off on it yet... we need to make sure we are getting that paperwork signed. But we need to record the details of it."
points: Rep-hiding (✅ OQ-5 resolved: route-hidden pre-ACCESS APPROVED by Rob — ship at the unlinked owners route now; real auth locks it at ACCESS rollout)

sections.heading: Rep view fix — pipeline click-through (Q42)
sections.decision: every card in the rep pipeline is one whole click target opening /rep/accounts/[id] — not just the name text. Rob: "you cant even click into them in the pipeline."

sections.heading: Build plan — ordered increments (≤6-min driver sized)
points: The increment-5 "company page ≠ person page" test, enumerated (testable)

docs.title: The Perfect CRM From the Rep's Seat — Research & Recommendations
docs.status: RESEARCH ONLY — nothing here is built by this doc
docs.lead: the perfect rep CRM is a finish-able daily queue that opens into a single account workspace where the rep can talk, send, and present without leaving the page — while the system does ALL the logging. Every product reps actually praise converges on that shape; every complaint converges on its absence. We already own most of the pieces.
